impact.affected_asset: HTTP/2 endpoint CPU and input-processing capacity
impact.attacker_capability: Cause an HTTP/2 endpoint to read and process arbitrary amounts of request header data, including data with asymmetric Huffman decoding cost
impact.security_effect: Availability degradation through arbitrary-volume HTTP/2 header-data processing

causal_trace.summary: A remote peer sends an excessive number of HTTP/2 CONTINUATION frames carrying request header data.

After request headers exceed MaxHeaderBytes, excess headers are not stored, but the endpoint continues parsing them; there was no stated bound on excess header frames processed for a request that will be rejected.

Maintaining HPACK state requires parsing and processing all received HEADERS and CONTINUATION frames; Huffman-encoded header data can impose substantially greater decoding work on the receiver than send effort.
The endpoint can be induced to read arbitrary amounts of header data associated with a request that is going to be rejected, causing unbounded input-processing work.

failure.operation: Parsing and processing unbounded excess HTTP/2 header data, including potentially costly Huffman decoding

primary_invariant.kind: bounded processing of rejected HTTP/2 request headers
primary_invariant.statement: Once a request exceeds MaxHeaderBytes and will be rejected, the endpoint must bound further excess-header-frame processing and close the connection at the limit.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The implementation continued parsing HEADERS and CONTINUATION frames to maintain HPACK state even though excess header data was not retained and the request would be rejected.

quality.review_notes: The Go vulnerability advisory and release metadata directly support the mechanism, affected ranges, and mitigation. The supplied CL artifact has no rendered diff and no regression-test or execution-result artifact was available, so no test oracle or observed reproducibility claim is made.

remediation.invariant_restored: The receiver limits the amount of excess header frames processed after request headers exceed the configured maximum, then closes the connection.
mitigation_classes: close the HTTP/2 connection after the excess-frame limit
